$comment: R1973 — WHAT THE REFERENCE DECLARES FOR A READER WHO CANNOT SEE THE SCREEN,
measured from the reference documents themselves rather than remembered.
The standing order for this reproduction has two halves: build what the
reference has and we lack, and do NOT delete what we have and it lacks.
The second half had no instrument. Nothing in this tree could say whether a
surface of ours is a reproduction or a second-stage improvement, so 'we are
ahead' was an assumption, and an assumption cannot tell being ahead from
having diverged.
MEASURED at R1973, over the reference documents this project reproduces:
the scope reference declares ZERO role attributes and ZERO aria-* state
attributes; the behaviour reference declares ZERO of each; the newest
integrated reference document declares FIVE attributes in thirty-one
megabytes — one role and four states. Reproduced by
grep -o 'role="[a-z]*"' <doc> | wc -l
grep -o 'aria-[a-z]*=' <doc> | wc -l
on the documents named in docs/SEED_PROMPT.md (they are outside the
repository and under NDA, so what is pinned here is the SHAPE and the
COUNT, in W3C vocabulary, and never a line of the documents).
=> the accessibility surface of this application is almost entirely SECOND
STAGE. That is not a licence to stop measuring it: the one role the
reference does declare is a reproduction obligation like any other, and it
is asserted by name. What the surplus figure buys is the other direction —
a round that quietly DELETED a voice would show up as the distance closing,
and before this nothing would have noticed.
Roles the reference declares, in W3C names. `tablist` is the whole list:
one occurrence, on the strip of view tabs.
`states` are the aria-* attributes it sets. They are STATES of a control
rather than roles, so they are pinned apart — a reader is told what a
thing IS by the first and what it is DOING by the second, and folding
them would make a count that cannot answer either question.
Deliberately NOT a pinned count of our own rows. `spec::VOICES` is the
declaration and the gate derives its size at test time; writing the
number here as well would be the same fact in two places, which is the
class this repository has 63 open debts about. What IS pinned is the
FLOOR: the reproduction is complete only while our surface is a strict
superset of the reference's, so the gate asserts every canon role is
reproduced and that the surplus is positive.
R2027 — AND THE RATCHET IS NOT A NUMBER EITHER, for the same reason.
'positive' has a floor of ONE, so 21 role kinds falling to 2 passed.
What replaces the missing count is `spec::VOICES`'s own `role` column:
r2027 asserts every declared region is ANNOUNCED WITH THE ROLE IT
DECLARES, so a voice kind can only leave by an edit to that table --
the same visibility every other column of it has, and still no count
in two files. Measured at R2027: that column had exactly one reader,
`main.rs` publishing it on the wire, and nothing had ever compared it
with the tree.
WARNING R2027 -- the two tables do NOT join on `tablist`, and that is a
fact rather than a gap. `spec::VOICES` is of regions the screen PAINTS;
the reference's one role sits on `shell.appbar.tabs`, a grouping node
with no box of its own. So the canon list is compared against the TREE
(r1973, r2027's last assertion) and never against that table -- adding
a row for it takes three gates red, which is how this was measured.
